scope: Hostile prompt injection protection and trust boundaries only; excludes memory retrieval/injection.
method: Read-only canonical source inspection, SHA-256 comparison, AST-isolated pure local function tests; only this requested report was written in clever-squid.

checks.expected: Mandatory content guard on untrusted outputs before reuse/handoff/side effects.
checks.observed: Source and deployed dist are byte-identical. execute.before checks only event.tool against writer_draft_internal, writer_repair_internal, semantic.execute_internal. No post-tool content gate, guard invocation, policy loading or P0/P2 execution receipt in this adapter. Other validation checks tool inputs/host identity, not hostile output content. Semantic execution is explicitly disabled.
checks.impact: Ordinary web/document/subagent tool names are not content-guarded by this hook. This is missing enforcement, not a demonstration that a model obeyed an attack.
checks.smallest_complete_fix: Integrate a mandatory untrusted-output gate before downstream consumption, with coverage and fail-closed execution receipts; a pre-tool name check alone is insufficient.

checks.expected: Runtime proves P0 and required P2 actually ran on each relevant untrusted input.
checks.observed: Guard points are policy instructions to run scripts, including an explicit no-DB labeling alternative. V2 exposes deterministic route/status calls, not automatic guard execution. In the inspected path invocation remains caller/orchestrator-driven; an available script or guard_required flag is not execution evidence.

checks.expected: ERROR, missing/unknown verdicts and unsuccessful subprocess exits cannot compose into PASS.
checks.observed: guard() blocks P0 only on exact FAIL, ignores both exit codes, and defaults P2 unknown/missing verdicts to success. Pure isolated tests reproduced PASS for P0 ERROR + P2 PASS, P0 PASS + empty P2 dict, and P2 PASS with exit 1. Explicit P0 FAIL blocks; explicit P2 DEGRADED returns ok=false. P0 timeout is uncaught and is not a structured BLOCK, but was not tested as a permissive caller outcome.
checks.smallest_complete_fix: Require explicit PASS and successful exit from both stages, reject malformed/unknown responses, and map execution exceptions/timeouts to structured non-success.

checks.expected: Unavailable bundled scanner cannot produce a clean scan.
checks.observed: researcher_core wrapper catches any bundled P0 import exception. Its fallback definitions are nested under the P2 import exception, and fallback _doc_analyze returns unconditional PASS without scanning. P2 import failure can replace even a successfully imported analyzer. scan_text also converts suspicion exceptions into low. This is wrapper behavior, not session_guard.py itself: the real scanner returns ERROR/nonzero for DB open failure. Actual deployment import failure was not induced.
checks.smallest_complete_fix: Remove unconditional PASS fallback; report unavailable/error and require caller rejection. Separate P0 and optional P2 import availability.

checks.expected: A P0 PASS is interpreted as no high configured-signature finding, not proof of safe content.
checks.observed: Finite signatures and contextual downgrades are used. Pure tests: bare 'ignore previous instructions' is high; adding 'table:' makes it low. Nested list-of-list strings are omitted by _iter_state_strings. Scanner takes the first matching signature/field and breaks even if low, so later high matches can be missed. Text parts are classified trusted solely by type; internal outputs receive no weak-RU checks. These are bounded scanner blindspots, not demonstrated successful hostile execution.

checks.expected: Required P2 checks cover all relevant untrusted material or report incomplete coverage as non-success.
checks.observed: Unresolved classifier results conservatively count as YES/FAIL, which is genuine fail-closed behavior for attempted classifications. However internal outputs skip P2; after default limit=50 further P0-clean untrusted parts are silently skipped. Long text is head/tail truncated, dropping the middle. Final PASS depends on findings, not complete coverage. Therefore P0+P2 PASS does not establish semantic analysis of all input.

checks.expected: Guard PASS proves actual scanning of the exact admitted untrusted artifact.
checks.observed: Real controls exist: registration hashes bytes, unknown origins reject, missing/non-PASS guards reject referenced guard_required artifacts in both submission and reducer, and a separate file-hash verification helper exists. But guard_artifact accepts a caller-provided verdict with default manual_guard, optional policy hash and empty findings; it does not invoke the scanner. Admissibility matches artifact_id and verdict, not an executed P0/P2 receipt bound to content hash. sanitize_artifact requires a known source and hashes derivative bytes but marks it guard_required=false without a scan. This establishes metadata gates, not cryptographic proof of scanning/sanitization. Requires a caller allowed to submit these events; no unauthorized access demonstrated.
checks.smallest_complete_fix: Bind admission to scanner-produced receipts containing artifact content hash, policy hash, required stages, coverage and successful execution; guard sanitized derivatives and retain source lineage.

checks.expected: A named audit CVE is applicable only with matching current vulnerable code evidence.
checks.observed: Audit (5) asserts CVE-2026-64651 applicability and sandbox-to-host authorization bypass. This review established neither that CVE's validity nor matching current vulnerable implementation. Three-name content-guard gap does not prove this separate authorization exploit.

checks.expected: Fresh bundled doc_guard P0 PASS on seven audits is distinguished from demonstrated defense.
checks.observed: Fresh seven-document P0 PASS was supplied by parent, not rerun here. It means no high finding by that scan, not absence of hostile content or verified enforcement. SHA-256 independently confirms reports (1),(2),(3) are exact duplicates, so seven files are five distinct contents. No hostile-protection claim matching searched terms was found in (6).

negative_case_tests.method: Canonical guard() AST function compiled alone with inert run_p0/run_p2 stubs; canonical session_guard module executed with non-main name, calling only pure helpers. python -B; no DB, subprocess scanner, network or provider call.

high_impact_gaps: No native output-content enforcement in current V2 adapter
Guard runner accepts malformed/error-stage success combinations
P0 wrapper has unconditional clean-result fallback
P2 silently omits excess parts and long-text middle
Factory metadata PASS/sanitized labels do not attest scanner execution
limits: No source/config edits, DB access, auth/key reads, web/model/paid calls, process/service changes or unsafe exploits.
Only the requested JSON artifact was created; no canonical state was intentionally changed.
No live host hook execution, model instruction-following attack, import-failure deployment test or end-to-end factory mutation was performed.
Canonical source and deployed dist files inspected; running host's actual loaded plugin identity was not queried.

Searches are navigation aids; relevant code ranges were read. One broad PowerShell search accidentally included non-Python paths and encountered locked daemon lock files; no content from those locks was read, and the search was replaced with extension-filtered Python inspection.
No quantitative bypass-rate or audit CVE claim is adopted as measured fact.
